title: A landed worktree that git calls a submodule stays
what: Find what makes git see a submodule in that worktree (a gitlink in the index, a leftover test repository, an ignored nested .git deeper than 4 levels), remove the leftover safely, and make relay land and the session-start cleanup name the cause and the next step instead of repeating the same line; a test that a worktree holding a nested repository from a test is either cleaned or reported once with what to do.
why: 29 Oct: since the land-test leak fix landed (wt/a-land-test-leaks-gate-scripts-that-load, merged), every relay land and every session start prints 'could not remove .worktrees/a-land-test-leaks-gate-scripts-that-load: working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed' and keeps the worktree and branch. `git submodule status` there prints nothing; no nested .git was found within 4 levels besides the worktree's own. Every landing repeats the line (principle 2: waste on every run), and relay doctor does not say what to do (principle 10).
failing_case: relay land of any branch prints 'kept .worktrees/a-land-test-leaks-gate-scripts-that-load: git refused to remove it' and the session start prints 'could not remove ... working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed', every time, with no next step.
pass_cases: the leftover worktree and its merged branch are gone after one relay land or relay doctor run
a merged worktree that git refuses to remove is reported once with its cause and the command that clears it
a merged worktree without nested repositories is removed as today
